claims.statement: Harvard-720: the four per-sentence result files (baseline, MRF, SEQ, Piper) contain 720 rows each with identical idx 0..719, text and order as harvard_testset_720.json; 0 non-finite UTMOSv2/WER/RTF, 0 audio <0.2 s, 0 empty ASR text; WAV durations match JSON.

verification.rationale: Checked: IDs/text/order, finiteness, WAV headers vs JSON durations, log has no Traceback. Not checked: audio content quality beyond scores.

claims.limitations: PyTorch CPU synthesis, Harvard-720, single draw per sentence.

claims.statement: Harvard-720 mean per-sentence RTF (PyTorch CPU): HiFi-GAN ResBlock2 0.04177, Parallel-IR 0.03388, Sequential-IR 0.03081, Piper 0.03916.

verification.rationale: Recomputed from per-sentence JSON. Timer = infer call only (excludes model load, phonemization, WAV write); RTF = time/duration per sentence then mean. Not controlled: no warm-up, one timing pass, torch threads not recorded at run time (default 12 observed now), Piper ran under torch 2.14.1 vs 2.13.0, an idle TensorBoard server was running.

claims.limitations: i7-14700, WSL Ubuntu 24.04, PyTorch CPU FP32; single run.

claims.statement: Sequential-IR is 9% faster than Parallel-IR on Harvard-720 (p=7e-37).

verification.rationale: 9.08% = RTF reduction 1-mean(SEQ)/mean(MRF); throughput gain 9.98%; ratio-of-sums reduction 9.34%. Wilcoxon (scipy default, two-sided, zero_method=wilcox) p=7.0e-37 replicates. Variation measured is between sentences only; benchmark repetition and training-run variance unmeasured; no warm-up.

claims.statement: On Harvard-720, Sequential-IR UTMOSv2 is lower than Parallel-IR by about 0.02 (p about 0.05).

verification.rationale: Mean diff -0.0237; Wilcoxon p=0.0471; MWU p=0.039; Holm over 15 tests p=0.094 (exploratory); paired bootstrap 95% [-0.0458, -0.0010] (exploratory). UTMOSv2 is a predicted score with unseeded random crops, one pass.

claims.limitations: UTMOSv2 predicted quality, not human MOS.

claims.statement: On Harvard-720, the WER difference between Sequential-IR and Parallel-IR is not statistically significant.

verification.rationale: Mean diff +0.0149 (WER fraction; SEQ worse). Wilcoxon p=0.0523 after dropping 323/720 zero differences; MWU p=0.080. Exploratory paired bootstrap CI [+0.0019, +0.0277] excludes 0. 'Not significant' is literally true for the reported test but does not imply equivalence.

claims.statement: Sequential-IR and Parallel-IR have comparable/equivalent speech quality.

verification.rationale: No equivalence/non-inferiority margin was pre-specified; both point estimates favour Parallel-IR; WER bootstrap CI excludes 0.

claims.statement: On Harvard-720, Sequential-IR vs Piper: 21% faster, UTMOSv2 +0.09, WER -0.05, all p<1e-10.

verification.rationale: 21.33% RTF reduction (27.1% throughput gain); UTMOSv2 +0.0936; WER -0.0525 as macro WER fraction = 5.25 percentage points absolute; Wilcoxon p = 8.1e-98 / 2.9e-13 / 4.7e-11. System-level comparison: different backbone, decoder, precision, data split, torch build.

claims.statement: Harvard-720 was not used to select checkpoints or the historical PTQ scope.

verification.rationale: Earliest 'harvard' mention in the inspected transcripts 2026-10-03T18:50:53Z; all Harvard files dated 2026-10-03/04; checkpoint callbacks finished 2026-09-02/09-17/09-29; PTQ graphs dated 2026-09-07..09-30. Not covered: activity outside the inspected sessions. Harvard results DID inform the Q02 claim wording proposed in this conversation.

claims.statement: Harvard-720 sentences do not overlap the LJSpeech training transcripts.

verification.rationale: 0 exact matches under two normalizations; 0 shared 6-grams; 0 identical phoneme-ID sequences; 37 sentences share a 4-gram and 7 a 5-gram (common phrases). Only against the 13,100 transcripts in dataset.jsonl; Piper's own training transcripts, audio similarity and scorer training data unchecked.

claims.statement: HiFi-GAN ResBlock2 and Sequential-IR were trained on the canonical 12,500/100/500 partition; Parallel-IR on a different random partition sharing 11,930/12,500 (95.44%) training utterances.

verification.rationale: Canonical corroborated by TensorBoard validation heads (9 phases) and kernel timestamps; MRF split reconstructed and corroborated against logged validation heads and the 2026-09-15 test manifest. Not a contemporaneous full-manifest hash.

claims.statement: Selected checkpoints are epoch 1489 (baseline), 1386 (MRF), 1442 (SEQ), chosen by ModelCheckpoint on val_loss_mel (min); Piper lj-med_1000 is epoch 999 with monitor=None.

verification.rationale: Epochs are zero-based metadata. Selection by validation mel L1 (x45), not by UTMOS/WER.

verification.rationale: Baseline v0 null, v1/v2 1.0 (hparams per session, Q03).

claims.statement: The baseline's SDP Log-flow exp clamp was changed from 30 to 10 (and an inference logw clamp added) before resuming from epoch 870.

verification.rationale: Recovered editor source + transcript timeline + resume log line; no runtime source hash.

claims.statement: Sequential-IR training code differs from Parallel-IR's: non-finite-gradient update skipping, SDP inference-health gating of best-checkpoint eligibility, duration-predictor edits, canonical split loader.

verification.rationale: Recovered source diff; SEQ logs contain skip messages (Q03). Confounder for any MRF-vs-SEQ causal attribution.

claims.statement: Decoder parameters: Sequential-IR 1.11M, Parallel-IR 1.15M, HiFi-GAN ResBlock2 1.66M.

verification.rationale: Exact 1,107,968 / 1,154,560 / 1,662,976; weight-norm folded; equals live count after remove_weight_norm.

claims.statement: Decoder compute: Sequential-IR 0.98 and Parallel-IR 1.23 GFLOPs per second of audio.

verification.rationale: Convention: Conv1d/ConvTranspose1d MACs x2 only (no activations/bias); T=86 frames (0.998 s): 0.9846 / 1.2306; per exact second 0.9861 / 1.2325. Baseline and Piper 3.90.

claims.statement: The Sequential-IR decoder is 33% smaller than Piper's; total inference parameters are 3.9% larger.

verification.rationale: 1-1,107,968/1,662,976 = 33.37%; 17,052,464/16,412,464-1 = 3.90%; boundary enc_p+dp+flow+dec, enc_q and discriminators excluded.

claims.statement: The HiFi-GAN ResBlock2 baseline decoder is identical to Piper's decoder.

verification.rationale: Same parameter count/shapes and MACs, but the activation before conv_post differs: LeakyReLU slope 0.1 (BanhmiTTS) vs F.leaky_relu default 0.01 (Piper).

claims.statement: Parallel-IR uses three parallel inverted-residual branches (depthwise kernels 3/5/7) averaged per stage; Sequential-IR uses two serial blocks (kernel 3, expansion 1) per stage; upsampling strides 8/8/4, kernels 16/16/8, channels 128/64/32.

verification.rationale: Current code + checkpoint hparams + state shapes (Q03 §3). Current code is not a runtime hash of training source.

claims.statement: The normalizing flow has 4 TransformerCouplingLayer+Flip pairs, each with a 1-layer 2-head self-attention (residual) before a 4-layer WaveNet (kernel 5), mean-only shift, run in reverse at inference; 8.29M params vs Piper 7.09M (Piper flow has no attention).

verification.rationale: Backbone description; not a novel contribution and not flow matching.

claims.statement: Historical ONNX Runtime FP32 RTF: Parallel-IR 0.0416 vs HiFi-GAN ResBlock2 0.0388 (Parallel-IR slower).

verification.rationale: Numbers reproduce, but mrf_fp32.onnx does not match checkpoint 1386 (Q05: 0/478 tensors) and MRF used its own 500-sentence manifest (21/500 shared). Cannot be attributed to MRF-1386.

verification.rationale: No final runs on the Q05 graphs; historical MRF graph source unknown; historical INT8 scopes differ (SEQ adds 40 QLinearMatMul).

claims.statement: In the inspected INT8 graphs the decoder remains FP32.

verification.rationale: No quantized op under /dec/ in baseline/MRF flow_enc_p_dp and SEQ int8 graphs. Does not show INT8 robustness of the decoder.
